To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the attenuation of LEMP radiated by indirect strokes is a significant phenomenon that can be taken into account for the evaluation of the lightning performance of power lines in urban areas; (2) the attenuation can be modeled through weighting functions that can be easily applied to the analytical expressions for LEMP in open terrain.
the lightning performance of an urban overhead power line is affected by the buildings nearby.
the lightning performance of an urban power distribution line can be accurately predicted with the proposed method.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the lightning protection of overhead power distribution lines in urban areas.
a new approach to the evaluation of the lightning performance of urban overhead power distribution lines.

the following aspects: (i) the evaluation of the attenuation of the lightning electromagnetic pulse by buildings, (ii) the identification of the weighting functions for the LEMP attenuation, and (iii) the evaluation of lightning performance of overhead power distribution lines in urban areas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of the buildings does not significantly affect the lightning performance of the power line, as long as the line is not located very close to them.
buildings nearby overhead lines reduce the lightning performance of the line, and that this reduction is more significant for the LEMP than for the direct strokes.
buildings nearby power distribution lines can reduce both direct and indirect lightning strikes to the line, but the reduction of the latter is more relevant than the former.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the buildings can reduce the lightning performance of an overhead power line, but only for a limited number of cases.
the lightning performance of a power line is affected by nearby buildings not only by means of the shielding effect, as expected, but also by means of the attenuation effect.
, for the configurations considered in this paper, a significant reduction of the lightning performance of the power line is observed when the buildings are included in the analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the buildings can significantly increase the lightning protection level of the line.
the presence of nearby structures can reduce the lightning performance of the line, but this reduction can be compensated by a suitable increase of the line clearance.
the buildings can reduce the lightning performance of the line by increasing the number of direct and indirect lightning strikes and by reducing the LEMP attenuation.
